title: Console Alerts: routing playbooks, SLO context cards, and post-incident navigation
creator: Ava Kim
description: Design and prototype a unified Alerts workflow in the Redwood Console that surfaces SLO context, enables routing to on-call teams, and embeds curated post-incident artifacts. The goal is to reduce time-to-context during incidents, make routing decisions explicit, and ensure postmortems and playbooks are discoverable from alert detail views.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity alert detail mock that shows SLO status, burn rate graph, and recent error traces
Routing UI for selecting primary/secondary on-call targets, with suggested targets based on history and service ownership
Embedded post-incident links area that can surface linked postmortems, runbooks, and relevant GitHub PRs
Prototype demonstrates handoff flow: alert -> acknowledge -> escalate -> create postmortem link
Design spec includes accessibility checks, responsive behaviors, and token-level cost/impact hint for noisy alerts
design_notes: We should avoid duplicating the existing Dashboard alert list; this is an alert detail/incident triage surface.
SLO context card will show current SLI, target, time window, and recent burn rate with an inline definition tooltip.
Routing suggestions are computed by backend, but UI needs affordances for override and temporary reroutes.
Post-incident area should allow attaching external links (Confluence/GDrive/GitHub) and optional summary text.
Consider single-column mobile-first layout for on-call mobile handoffs; hide dense charts behind an expander on small viewports.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Surface only top-3 suggested on-call targets to avoid choice paralysis; allow manual search for others.
Trade-off: Inline transcripts vs. link-out — chose link-out for large logs to keep alert view performant.
Decision: Use condensed sparklines for token-cost hints rather than full token-level table to reduce cognitive load.
Trade-off: Automatic postmortem creation vs. link suggestion — prototype implements link suggestion only to avoid forcing workflows.
user_research_findings: On-call engineers consistently wanted one-click routing to a team alias instead of individual names.
SREs wanted SLO context pinned above the fold — they check SLOs first during triage.
Product owners requested links to the last related postmortem to speed RCA when regressions recur.

open_risks: Backend APIs for suggested routing and postmortem lookup are not yet finalized; prototyping used mocked responses.
Audit log requirement may add latency to routing operations if implemented synchronously.
Too many cross-links could distract triage; we need to measure click-through in usability tests.
engineering_handoff_notes: Tokens: provide compressed sparklines data at 64px width with 10 points max for performance.
Routing: UI will call GET /api/v1/alerts/{id}/suggested_routes and PATCH /api/v1/alerts/{id}/route for overrides.
Attachments: support ACLs and signed URLs for external storage; include attachment metadata in audit events.
Accessibility: keyboard-first flow for acknowledge/escalate actions and ARIA labels for SLO definition tooltips.
